title: UT’s $25 million health AI project has big ambitions and unanswered questions
key_facts: The University of Texas System is setting up UT REAL Health AI, a $25 million state-funded initiative to manage and develop AI tools across its medical schools and hospitals, including MD Anderson Cancer Center and UTMB.

A UT REAL slideshow obtained through an open records request counts 571 AI use cases across eight medical schools and hospitals, 12% of them generative AI, with another 150 AI applications in production.
Internal documents say tools will be inventoried, security risks and purpose scrutinized, and benefits or harms monitored; a safety signal at one hospital would trigger a system-wide review.

Publicly available details are sparse; AI expert Numa Dhamani asks whether personal health information will be collected, how vendors protect data and how problems would be handled, and warns a centralized platform could be a cyberattack target.
The initiative's leaders either could not be reached or declined to answer questions; UT plans to partner with a vendor for AI management, but it is unclear whether an agreement exists.
UT REAL gave a $300,000 grant to expand UT Southwestern's AI system for grading medical-student exams to five other medical schools; early versions saved 980 grading hours, an 87.5% reduction.
Brian Anderson of the Coalition for Health AI says few institutions worldwide are doing this and UT is one of them.
quote_evidence: Publicly available details about the $25 million state-funded UT REAL program remain sparse, leaving one AI expert with questions about whether personal health information will be collected as part of the initiative, and how problems with AI’s performance would be handled, among other issues.
Among eight medical schools and hospitals, there are 571 AI “use cases,” or real-world scenarios in which the technology has been applied, according to the presentation.
UT plans to partner with a vendor to help with AI management, internal records show, but it’s not clear whether an agreement has been reached.
why_it_matters_hint: One of the biggest public health systems in the US is trying to track and oversee every AI tool it uses, but key details on data and responsibility are unanswered.
event_date: Not stated; Houston Chronicle published 2 Oct 2026.
notes: Based on internal UT documents and open-records emails seen by the Chronicle; UT leaders did not comment. The article does not give a launch date for UT REAL.
